story_type: aircraft carrier shock trials, 40,000-pound underwater blasts beside the ship
hook: 40,000 pounds of explosives, on purpose, next to a carrier.
narration: That blast was forty thousand pounds of explosives, set off on purpose beside an aircraft carrier.
This is USS Gerald R. Ford, in the Atlantic Ocean, in the summer of 2021.
In shock trials, each charge goes off closer to the ship, to prove it can keep operating in combat.
[short pause] Inside, sailors braced against the bulkheads.
Water carries a blast's shock far better than air does.
outcome: Ford withstood three 40,000 pound blasts and completed its shock trials.
title: 40,000 pound blasts next to a carrier
description:
In 2021, the aircraft carrier USS Gerald R. Ford completed Full Ship Shock Trials in the Atlantic Ocean, withstanding three 40,000-pound underwater blasts released progressively closer to the ship. The final event took place off Jacksonville, Florida, on Aug. 8, 2021.

Footage: U.S. Navy video by Petty Officer 3rd Class Zachary Melvin, USS Gerald R. Ford (CVN 78), via DVIDS: https://www.dvidshub.net/video/809395/ford-successfully-completes-shock-trials
